$comment: Single source of truth for every R package the app cares about.
Consumed by shared/optional-packages.ts (app + IPC allow-list), by the three
scripts/vendor-r-runtime.* scripts (Windows and Linux read the CRAN names,
macOS still the conda names), and by r-scripts/setup.R (the user installs
their own R path).
tests/unit/r-packages-manifest.test.ts fails if any consumer drifts from this file.
bundled = every package any analysis uses. The vendored runtime carries all of
them (signed with the rest of the runtime), so a user who installs the
packaged app installs nothing and needs no internet for R. Until 0.2.28
eleven of them were optional, downloaded on demand from the R Packages
manager; that left unsigned DLLs (Smart App Control) and a first-use wait,
and the manager was removed (2026-10-11).
Most of the first group are R recommended set, which every stock CRAN
install ships but conda-forge r-base does NOT.
conda is the conda-forge package name; recommended marks the ones
r-recommended pulls in as a group.
Windows R runtime source (scripts/vendor-r-runtime-win.ps1) and the package
repository every R package install uses — the vendored runtimes AND every
in-app install (r-bridge.ts installRPackage: the setup dialog for a user's own
R, the repair of a damaged runtime, the R terminal's Packages pane). The
repository is a dated Posit Package Manager snapshot: the same URL returns the
same package versions (with Windows/macOS binaries) forever, which is what keeps
builds reproducible. Linux builds the same R (SAI_R_VERSION, default = windowsR)
on conda-forge's toolchain and compiles the packages from this snapshot. macOS
is the exception: vendor-r-runtime-mac.sh still ships conda-forge's R 4.3 and
conda packages, so a macOS build is NOT the R the other platforms validate —
moving it to CRAN's R + this snapshot is the first macOS task.
Changing either value = an R upgrade: rerun scripts/compare-r-versions.cjs and
the SPSS parity suites before shipping (roadmap.md, 2026-10-10).
Packages no analysis uses but an R user expects on day one in the R
terminal (2026-10-21: `library(ggplot2)` failed in a fresh install). The
vendored runtimes carry them; they are NOT part of the first-run check for
a system-R user nor of the analysis install allow-list. Kept BEFORE the
bundled list: setup.R reads everything after that key as the list.
Measured on Windows (R 4.6.1, 2026-09-01 snapshot): these three + their
dependencies add ~15 MB compressed to the installer. car was left out —
its dependency tree (pbkrtest, doBy, forecast, quantreg …) alone adds
~19 MB; it installs from the Packages panel.

bundled.use: Ordinal regression: location, scale and nominal models
Exact / Monte Carlo nonparametric tests (tied data)
Dunnett and general linear hypothesis post hoc
